method: Opened official references and read relevant guidance/legal provisions using web browsing. Approved teaching text preserved.

sources.finding: Travel volume, fuel mix, energy efficiency and electrification affect greenhouse-gas emissions; no numerical savings added.
Exhaust and wear particles from brakes, tyres and road surfaces are distinct sources.
Tyre-road interaction dominates at higher speeds; quieter electric propulsion does not eliminate all noise.
7 January 2026 notice confirms revised weighting for new registrations from 2026, reflecting electric and combustion operation; no journey-consumption guarantee.
Correct tyre pressure, speed limits and removing unused roof equipment are recommended. No fixed percentage saving or universal gear/engine-speed claim.
Chapters 4 and 5 address travel purpose, modes, companions, route, circumstances and personal factors; self-assessment in chapters 2, 4 and 5 supports reflection.

National classes and municipality decisions distinguished. Class 2 petrol/spark-ignition Euro 5/6 versus diesel Euro 6; class 3 light vehicles checked against exact legal text rather than extending heavy plug-in-hybrid permission.

Chapter 3 sections 2 and 14 support following distance and safe speed/control. Chapter 4 sections 22–24a supports class-specific environmental-zone criteria; light gas vehicles use Euro 6 table-2 limits. Exemptions and vehicle documentation remain qualified. No named municipal boundary is asserted.

Official service provides regulations including amendments and a register for rules effective on a selected date. Availability verified; no actual city-specific access decision is needed or claimed in this hypothetical lesson.
